name: LAKEVIEW PARK
description:
Lakeview Park Campground is located on Bull Shoals Lake. Set in the scenic Ozark Mountains of northern Arkansas and southern Missouri, the lake has hundreds of miles of lake arms and coves perfect for boating, water sports, swimming, fishing and scuba diving. 
  
The lake also appeals to birders, naturalists, hunters and visitors seeking a fun and peaceful place to relax along the water.Lakeview Park Campground offers 78 campsites, all with electric hookups, along with two large group shelters. 
  
Amenities like hot showers, flush toilets, a dump station, boat ramp, swimming area and playground make this campground popular among boaters, fishermen and families.Lakeview is a large park with wooded campsites on a bluff overlooking the water. The lake and surrounding mountains are popular year-round as each season unfolds a new panorama. Summer contrasts lush green hardwoods and cedar glades against towering rocky bluffs and unusual rock formations. Fall foliage presents the renowned "flaming fall revue."
  
Watching and photographing wildlife can be enjoyed in developed and undeveloped areas alike. Each year more than 100 bald eagles winter in the Bull Shoals area.Cruise around the lake to see nearly 20 other public parks and hundreds of miles of undeveloped land and coves around the lake, which include additional swim areas and 11 marinas.The lake is a water sports paradise. Marinas offer boat rentals, supplies and guides for hire. Year-round fishing tournaments keep fishermen active as they seek out 12-pound bass and other species ranging from pan fish to walleye. The lake holds several state fishing records and the nearby White River is a premier trout fishery in the central United States.
  
There is also a 1.5-mile nature trail that begins in the campground.

name: LEAD HILL
description:
Lead Hill Campground is a splendid, sizable campground with plenty of waterfront sites along the shores of Bull Shoals Lake.   
The lake, renowned as a haven for water sports enthusiasts, boasts nearly 1,000 miles of shoreline along the Arkansas and Missouri border.Year-round fishing tournaments keep fishermen active as they seek out 12-pound bass. The lake also attracts birders, naturalists, hikers, scuba divers and those who come for all types of motorboat sports.Most of the 75 campsites have canopies over picnic tables for cooling shade, and each one is equipped with electric hookups. The campground also has two group campsites, a playground, designated swim area and a marina. 
Lead Hill is on the Arkansas side of Bull Shoals, which stretches across the border of Arkansas and Missouri. Bull Shoals Lake, formed by a dam built in 1951, stems from the White River in the Ozark Mountains, and eventually flows into the Mississippi.Cruise around the lake to see the many public parks operated by the Army Corps of Engineers. These parks cover additional swim areas, 11 marinas and several hundred miles of undeveloped land and coves.

name: LITTLE COON CREEK PARK
description: Little Coon Creek Campground is located on Gillham Lake in southwestern Arkansas on the Cossatot River. The rugged terrain around the lake creates stunning views and provides for many opportunities for boating, fishing, hunting, and swimming.Visitors enjoy the lake for its vast boating opportunities, and a boat ramp is provided for easy water access.  Anglers will find smallmouth, largemouth, and spotted bass, saugeye, crappie, channel and flathead catfish and various species of sunfish in the river. Hunting is allowed north of Little Coon Creek Park and on the eastern shore of the lake. Check with the Arkansas Game and Fish for Season Dates and Regulations. Lake maps are also available from any Park Attendant at the lake.Little Coon Creek provides 10 campsites and a group picnic shelter; each site has water and 50-amp electric hookups available. Additional amenities include hot showers with restrooms, a boat ramp with a handicap accessible fishing pier, a playground and a dump station nearby.Gillham Lake spans 1,370 surface acres and boasts 36 miles of shoreline. The Dam was completed in 1975 and stems from the Cossatot River, which has been designated as a National Wild and Scenic River.The Cossatot River State Park-Natural Area and the Queen Wilhelmina State Park are both within driving distance just north of Gillham Lake. Both of these attractions offer great scenery, hiking, and interpretive programs that are fun for all ages.

name: LOST BRIDGE NORTH
description:
Lost Bridge North Campground sits along the vast shores of Beaver Lake in the Ozark Mountains of Northwest Arkansas, offering spacious and sunny campsites and an abundance of recreational activities. 
Lost Bridge North Campground has large campsites with plenty of shade and room for activities, and is steps away from the lake shore. Fire rings, picnic areas, drinking water and flush toilets all make for a comfortable camping getaway.Towering limestone bluffs, natural caves and a variety of trees and flowering shrubs surround Lost Bridge North Campground, making it an ideal retreat for outdoor enthusiasts.
  
Beaver Lake and Dam, completed in 1966, was constructed in the White River Basin and boasts 449 miles of beautiful shoreline at the top of the conservation pool.
  
Although the dam was originally built for flood control, hydroelectric power and public water supply, it has also created a popular recreational oasis.Several marinas are located around the lake, offering groceries, fuel, boat rentals and storage, fishing guides and camping supplies. Click  here  for more information.Fishing opportunities are plentiful near Lost Bridge North Campground. Beaver Lake has more than 28,000 surface acres of water, and anglers can try their luck at catching large and small-mouth bass, crappie, bream, white bass, stripers, and channel or spoon-bill catfish. Just below the dam, the cold waters of the upper White River provide a perfect habitat for pole-bending rainbow and record-size German brown trout. 
  
Several trails snake throughout the Ozark Mountains, offering peaceful hiking, biking and wildlife viewing opportunities for visitors.
  
Hunters will find game plentiful in northwest Arkansas. A mixture of hardwood and evergreen forest provides a good home to many different species of wildlife. While Beaver Lake is conveniently located near several population centers, within a short driving distance hunters can find remote areas filled with upland game animals such as deer, rabbits and squirrels.
  
Many other sports and activities await campers, including boating, swimming, picnicking, scuba diving, water skiing, spelunking and sightseeing.

name: Lake Greeson
description: Lake Greeson, AR, on the Little Missouri River, has many hunting and fishing opportunities as well as camping, swimming and boating.   The lake is a wintering site for bald eagles.  A nature trail allows the visitor to reach the site of a cinnabar mine.  The 31-mile-long cycle trail and the Chimney Rock geological formation are also located at Lake Greeson.

name: Lake Ouachita
description: Lake Ouachita, AR is located on the Ouachita River near the resort spa of Hot Springs.  Its crystal-clear waters make the lake a popular site for scuba diving.  There are numerous camping, fishing and swimming opportunities at the lake as well as concessions with marinas, motels, restaurants and horseback riding.  There is a boating trail for viewing geological formations on the shoreline.

name: Little Pines Campground
description: Little Pines Recreation Area is located on the shoreline of 960-acre Lake Hinkle in the Poteau Mountain area of the Ouachita National Forest, approximately 12 miles west of Waldron, Arkansas. Built in a former pine plantation, the campground offers nine level campsites with shade, water, and electrical service.  The recreation area provides opportunities for camping, picnicking, boating, and fishing. A boat ramp adjacent to the campground provides lake access, and a courtesy dock and fishing pier are available. Lake Hinkle is managed by the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission. Anglers should consult current Commission regulations and licensing requirements before fishing.  Visitors can also explore hiking, mountain-biking, and off-highway-vehicle trails within a few miles of the campground. A campground host may be available to assist visitors and answer questions about the area. Waldron offers groceries, restaurants, medical services, fuel, and other supplies.   Campsite Locations   All nine campsites are within surrounded by Lake Hinkle on three sides. Campsites are categorized by their position within the campground:     Lakeside sites—5, 6, 7, 8, and 9:  Located on the lake side of the campground, with no other campsites between these sites and the shoreline.     Interior sites—1, 2, 3, and 4:  Located within the interior portion of the campground, slightly farther from the shoreline.    Vegetation, terrain, and seasonal lake levels may affect water views and shoreline access. A lakeside designation does not necessarily indicate a direct water view or direct access from the campsite. All campsites have sidewalk access to the boat docks and fishing pier.Little Pines Campground is a convenient base for exploring the Ouachita National Forest and the Waldron area.     Scott County Museum of History:  Located in downtown Waldron, the museum features exhibits highlighting Scott County’s communities, people, and cultural history.     Ouachita National Recreation Trail:  This long-distance trail crosses the Ouachita Mountains through Arkansas and Oklahoma. A segment follows the crest of Fourche Mountain and offers opportunities for hiking and backcountry exploration.     Belle Starr Multi-Use Trail:  Formerly known as the Poteau Mountain Multi-Use Trail, this 22.6-mile loop travels through varied forest and mountain terrain. The trail accommodates hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, and designated off-highway-vehicle use.     Fourche Mountain Trail:  This multi-use trail provides opportunities for hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, and designated off-highway-vehicle use in the Ouachita National Forest.    Trail surfaces, difficulty, seasonal access, and permitted uses vary. Before visiting, obtain current Forest Service maps and check trail conditions, closures, and off-highway-vehicle requirements. Contact the Scott County Museum of History directly for current hours and admission information.Little Pines Recreation Area offers camping, picnicking, hiking, boating, and fishing along 960-acre Lake Hinkle, which is managed by the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission. A boat ramp, courtesy dock, and fishing pier provide access to the lake, while a short hiking trail begins in the day-use area. Additional hiking, mountain-biking, and designated off-highway-vehicle trails are available within a few miles of the campground.  Visitors should consult the Arkansas Game and Fish Commission for current fishing-license requirements and regulations. Trail users should check current Forest Service maps, conditions, and vehicle requirements before heading out.Little Pines Campground has nine reservable single campsites along the shoreline of Lake Hinkle. All sites are back-in; no pull-through sites are available. Each campsite includes a paved parking spur, picnic table, fire ring, lantern post, and electrical and water connections. Flush toilets, showers, and a trailer dump station are also available.  Boating facilities include a ramp for launching and retrieving boats, a courtesy dock, and docks for registered campers to moor boats during their stay. A fish-cleaning station is located near the boat ramp. An adjacent day-use area includes a large picnic pavilion and swimming area.Little Pines Campground is located along the shoreline of 960-acre Lake Hinkle in the Poteau Mountain area of the Ouachita Mountains. Developed within a former pine plantation, the campground features level campsites and a shaded forest setting. An adjacent boat ramp provides convenient access to the lake.
